card.name: Capitalized words before a hyphen in warnings
card.fires_on: The first part of an all-caps compound or word in boxed warnings and caution text, right before a hyphen or the rest of the word, such as ALL-CAUSE, CROSS-HYPERSENSITIVITY, LOSS-OF-FUNCTION.

modes.label: Hyphenated warning terms
modes.description: An all-caps word that opens a hyphenated compound in a warning heading or caution.
modes.example: CAUTION SHOULD BE EXERCISED BECAUSE<< CROSS>>-HYPERSENSITIVITY AMONG

modes.label: Inside all-caps words
modes.description: A piece in the middle of a capitalized word, split before the rest of it.
modes.example: UNTIL THE ETIOLOGY IS D<<ETER>>MINED WITH CERTAINTY.

card.writes: It promotes forms of the word practice and suppresses the letter P, which gives no clear link to the contexts.
card.plain: It fires on the opening part of capitalized warning terms that continue after a hyphen, like ALL-CAUSE or CROSS-sensitivity.
